findings.F1: The next-day move after a day grows step by step with the size of that day's fall in units of the 30-day swing, in every profile together (excess over the coin's mean, cases of a day taken together). After z ≤ -2 it is +1.89 % (t 2.10, 166 cases on 63 days); after -2 to -1 it is +0.71 % (t 1.79, 265 days); after -1 to -0.3 it is +0.18 % (t 0.75); after -0.3 to +0.3 it is -0.24 % (t -1.36).
findings.F2: Up days of any size are followed only by a drift-level shortfall, with no grading. The next-day excess is -0.23 %, -0.20 % and -0.21 % after z of 0.3–1, 1–2 and >2 (t -1.20, -0.74, -0.41). The reversal the tested idea bets on (fading rises) is the weak side, which matches its slope of -2.4e-05 and its t of 1.51.
findings.F3: The fall rebound is not confined to falling markets. Next-day excess after z of -2 to -1 is +0.73 % in falling (t 2.26, 229 cases), +1.23 % in rising (t 2.63, 164 cases) and -1.29 % in choppy (43 cases). After z ≤ -2 it is +1.50 % in falling (66 cases) and +1.32 % in rising (22 cases); these t are not day-clustered.
findings.F4: The rebound after large falls is large against the cost of a trade. +1.89 % per case after z ≤ -2 is about 10 times the 0.19 % cost, and +0.71 % after -2 to -1 is about 3.7 times. By comparison, the tested idea's total move is 0.7 times the cost.
findings.F5: Most of the rebound shows on the first day. On a non-overlapping 2-day grid, the excess after z ≤ -2 is +0.97 % (t 0.77, 37 days) and after -2 to -1 is +1.01 % (t 1.36), no larger than the one-day move.
findings.F6: A close near the day's low is followed by a higher next day: +0.58 % in the lowest fifth of the range (t 3.50, 1092 cases) against -0.36 % in the top fifth (t -2.69). In a joint regression with the scaled return, neither stays significant (z t -1.43, close location t -1.34), so this is the same fall-rebound effect, not a separate one.
findings.F7: The negative link between a day's scaled move and the next day's scaled excess appears only in agitated markets. The correlation is -0.18 in falling agitated (t -4.0, 492 cases) and -0.28 in choppy agitated (t -2.85, 106 cases), against +0.02 in falling calm and +0.01 in choppy calm. However, the day-clustered reversal by |z| in agitated markets is not graded: 0.89 % at |z| < 0.5 and 0.16 % at |z| > 2.

ideas.idea: After a down day, a coin rises over the next day, and the larger that day's fall in units of its 30-day daily-return swing, the larger the next day's rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys the day after an outsized fall rather than shorting the day after an outsized rise, because the overshoot that is repaid next day is the selling one.
ideas.name: scaled fall next-day rebound

ideas.idea: In a falling market, after a down day, a coin rises over the next day, and the larger that day's fall in units of its 30-day daily-return swing, the larger the next day's rise.
ideas.consequence: In a downtrend, forced selling on an outsized down day is partly repaid the next day, so a trader buys it rather than adding to shorts.
ideas.name: falling market fall rebound
